records.label: 5-year-old female patient
quotes: Here, we report a 5-year-old female patient with cutaneous syndactyly, developmental delay, and pulmonary hypertension. Exome analysis showed a previously undescribed de novo heterozygous mutation in the CACNA1C gene, p.Arg1024Gly.
this patient is the first to exhibit syndactyly and to carry a CACNA1C mutation but to not have QT prolongation

quotes: Trio ES revealed a heterozygous de novo variant in CACNA1C (NM_000719.6: c.4087G>A, p.V1363M).
She was found to have profound axial and appendicular hypotonia, laryngomalacia with stridor, bilateral clubbed feet, bilateral 3–4 finger and 2–3 toe syndactyly, and camptodactyly.
Her seizures started within a few hours of birth with numerous subtle tonic seizures as well as prolonged tonic and tonic-myoclonic seizures per day.

quotes: The first was a heterozygous CACNA1C splice site variant (NM_000719.6: c.3717+1_3717+2insA) that was paternally inherited.
This worsened following discharge and an ECHO demonstrated TOF which was surgically repaired at 2 months of age.
At 8 months, she had mild developmental delays. By 12 months, she spoke 10 words and first walked. Her neurologic exam showed mild diffuse hypotonia.

quotes: Her father, who also carried the splice site variant in CACNA1C, had a congenital ventricular septal defect and aortic valve stenosis which was repaired at age 2.5 months.
In addition, he had learning disabilities requiring individualized education program at school and attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). By 18 years, he developed seizures.

His craniofacial features were similar to his daughters and shared many commonalities to described individuals with Timothy syndrome, including low-set ears, thin vermillion border of the upper lip, premaxillary underdevelopment, and a round face.

notes.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) described a CACNA1C-related neurological disorder that variably included developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism, epilepsy, hypotonia, and ataxia. Significant cardiac abnormalities and the classic features of Timothy syndrome were absent in all but one of the 25 individuals.
quotes: In conclusion, we delineate the phenotypic spectrum of a CACNA1C-related neurological disorder variably associated with developmental delay, intellectual disability, autism, epilepsy, hypotonia, and ataxia.
Significant cardiac abnormalities were absent in all but one of the individuals in our cohort at most recent follow-up.

notes.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) found that all 14 individuals with de novo nontruncating variants had developmental delay or intellectual disability. Nine were nonverbal, 12 had hypotonia, 10 had epilepsy with onset from 2 months to 8 years, and 12 had orthopedic abnormalities, including clubfoot, hip dysplasia, syndactyly, and joint hypermobility.
quotes: All 14 individuals with non-truncating variants have a history of developmental delays or intellectual disability.
Ten of 14 individuals in our cohort with non-truncating variants have epilepsy, with onset ranging from 2 months to 8 years.
Orthopedic abnormalities were common in individuals with non-truncating variants (n = 12/14).

notes.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) observed that individuals with truncating CACNA1C variants had milder, more selective deficits than those with nontruncating variants. Ten of 11 had delayed expressive language, early motor development was essentially normal in all but 1, 5 of 11 had autism, and only 1 had seizures. Penetrance and expressivity among family members appeared to be variable.
quotes: These individuals as a group appeared to have more selective developmental abnormalities involving expressive language; 10/11 individuals in this group had delayed expressive language, whereas early motor development was essentially normal in all but one patient.
Finally, there appeared to be variable penetrance and expressivity of features amongst different family members with truncating variants.

notes.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) identified heterozygous CACNA1C variants in 25 individuals from 22 families: 13 de novo missense variants, 1 de novo in-frame deletion, and truncating variants in 11 individuals from 8 families. None of the variants were present in gnomAD, 1000 Genomes, or the Exome Variant Server.
quotes: Thirteen unrelated individuals have missense variants in CACNA1C, one individual has an in-frame deletion, and 11 individuals from 8 families have predicted truncating variants, including one canonical splice variant.
All the non-truncating variants and all but three of the truncating variants occurred de novo.

notes.statement: In patch-clamp studies in HEK293 cells, Rodan et al. (2021) found that the L1408V variant reduced current density to about 30% of wildtype with unchanged protein expression. L657F produced about a 2-fold increase in current and in protein level, L614P produced a modest, nonsignificant current increase, and L614R had no significant effect.
quotes: The Leu1408Val variant appears to have a clear effect on overall channel activity, as current density associated with this variant was significantly reduced to approximately 30% of control, but the protein expression was unchanged.
The gain-of-function effect of the Leu657Phe variant is most likely explained by an increase in protein expression, as both the current density and protein level increased by approximately 2-fold.
The p.Leu614Arg variant did not appear to confer any statistically significant change in current or properties of voltage-dependent gating

notes.statement: Rodan et al. (2021) suggested that CACNA1C may be haploinsufficient (gnomAD pLI of 1.0). They proposed that the more severe phenotype in patients with missense loss-of-function variants, compared with patients with whole-gene or exonic deletions, would better support a dominant-negative effect.
quotes: This is further supported by constraint analysis on the gnomAD dataset, demonstrating an observed/expected ratio of for predicted loss-of-function variants of 0.05 and probability of loss-of-function intolerance (pLI) score of 1.0.

The more severe neurodevelopmental and epilepsy phenotype in patients with missense, predicted loss-of-function variants compared to those with whole gene/exonic deletions would better support a dominant-negative effect.

notes.statement: Bozarth et al. (2018) modeled the V1363M variant on a predicted 3D structure of Cav1.2. It lies in the fifth transmembrane helix of domain IV, faces the pore-forming sixth helix, and is in direct contact with A1473G, a Timothy syndrome variant. The authors suggested that the larger methionine residue likely disrupts the sixth helix and affects channel gating or calcium transmission.
quotes: The fifth TMH in each domain is packed directly against the sixth TMH, and position 1363 is facing towards the sixth TMH. A change from valine to methionine, a larger residue, likely disrupts the protein structure in the sixth TMH, affecting the gating or calcium transmission of Cav1.2.
V1363M (colored in magenta) is in direct contact with a variant associated with severe neurologic disease, A1473G (colored in yellow).

notes.statement: Bozarth et al. (2018) noted that their patient with the de novo V1363M variant had many hallmark features of Timothy syndrome, including cutaneous syndactyly, dysmorphic features and sleep disturbances, but no cardiac abnormalities. She differed from previously reported individuals in having severe refractory neonatal-onset epilepsy, no neurodevelopmental progression, and a recognizable EEG pattern of diffuse fast activity.
quotes: Patient 1 had many hallmark features of Timothy Syndrome including cutaneous syndactyly, dysmorphic features, and sleep disturbances; however, she lacked cardiac abnormalities.

Her presentation differs from previously reported individuals in regard to her severe refractory epilepsy of neonatal onset, lack of neurodevelopment, and recognizable EEG patterns of diffuse fast activity.

notes.statement: In the patient with the V1363M variant, Bozarth et al. (2018) found that seizures did not respond to multiple antiepileptic drugs. Topiramate and valproic acid gave a small reduction, and clobazam reduced seizures from numerous per day to fewer than 10 per day and improved sleep.
quotes: At 7 months, clobazam was started, which significantly reduced her seizure burden from numerous tonic seizures per day to less than 10 per day and improved sleep duration of 8 to 10 hours at night.

notes.statement: Kosaki et al. (2018) noted that their patient was the first to have syndactyly and a CACNA1C mutation without QT prolongation, a feature long considered obligatory for Timothy syndrome.
quotes: To our knowledge, this patient is the first to exhibit syndactyly and to carry a CACNA1C mutation but to not have QT prolongation, which has long been considered an obligatory feature of Timothy syndrome.
